All 12 steps and all named supplier statements checked. For connected G, exponential closure has full tangent dimension and hence equals irreducible G; finite radical weights are invariant under connected conjugation, so [g,r] is nilpotent in a triangular basis. Its generated closure is connected normal and has fixed vectors by Lie triangularisation and trivial polynomial Ga characters. Reductivity kills it. Central nilpotent Jordan parts lie in the exponential closure: exponential-polynomial independence separates each exponent coefficient, allowing independent nilpotent parameter u. A nonzero nilpotent part would give a central closed Ga, so the centre acts through a diagonal algebraic subgroup; character weight spaces and Weyl complements give complete reducibility. Conjugate normal unipotent subgroups have successive nonzero fixed spaces, and finite component averaging extends complements. AC is used for sum-of-simples splitting; naturality gives exactness on invariants and invariant-algebra linearity. The faithful-module converse and polynomial log curves establish hereditary unipotence and both identity-component directions. Haar translation invariance, dense K, and compact finite-dimensional convex hull prove conditional clause (iv), including V=0. Milne Proposition 22.41/Theorem 22.42/Corollary 22.43, pp. 478–479, independently support the conclusion; Brion 1.23 p. 8 omits compact existence, which this item does not claim. Statement unchanged. Reviewed all five steps and exact cited dependencies, including the independently checked current batch-15 supplier chain. Connected orbits are irreducible locally closed and obey the dimension/boundary formula. For disconnected G, reduced stabilizers have finitely many clopen cosets; (Gx)^0 lies in (G^0)x, so equal dimensions hold. Finite connected-group orbits have common dimension d. If one meets another closure it lies entirely in it; equal dimensions force equal closures, contradicting disjoint dense opens. Thus each O_i misses the other closures, the full orbit is open in the finite closed union, and every closure component has dimension d. Boundary connected orbits, hence finite unions forming full orbits, have smaller dimension. Minimum among nonnegative orbit dimensions gives a closed orbit in every closure. Dimension-zero groups and stabilizers equal to G work; x excludes empty X. Statement unchanged, so no downstream interface repair is required.
